'''Jaxson Reed Hayes''' (born May 23, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]].

==High school career==
Hayes attended [[Moeller High School]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.myrtlebeachonline.com/sports/high-school/beach-ball-classic/article191728964.html|title=Beach Ball Notebook: Moeller’s Jaxson Hayes quickly growing into newfound stardom|website=myrtlebeachonline}}</ref> He grew from six feet as a freshman to 6'11 as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.themonitor.com/2018/12/19/texas-freshman-jaxson-hayes-rising-hoops-star/|title=Texas freshman Jaxson Hayes is rising hoops star|agency=Associated Press|date=December 19, 2018|publisher=}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 12 points, seven rebounds and four blocks per game. He committed to the [[University of Texas]] to play college basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/moeller-basketball-standout-jaxson-hayes-announces-college-decision|title=Moeller basketball star announces college choice|date=September 29, 2017|website=WCPO}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2017/09/29/and-winner-moellers-hayes-texas/718011001/|title=And the winner for Moeller's Hayes is Texas|website=Cincinnati.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hayes father, [[Jonathan Hayes]], played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and is currently the tight ends coach of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/11/02/jaxson-hayes-fran-fraschilla-praises-texas-long-term-nba-prospect/1857833002/|title=Fran Fraschilla: Jaxson Hayes is best long-term NBA prospect of more than 20 college teams|website=Cincinnati.com}}</ref>His mother, Kristi (Kinne) played basketball at Drake University (1991-95) and earned honorable mention Kodak All-American accolades and Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year honors as a senior (1994-95) Kristi recorded 3,406 career points during her four years (1987-91) at Jefferson-Scranton High School (Jefferson, Iowa) Kristi previously served as an assistant women’s basketball coach at Oklahoma, Iowa and Southern Illinois-Carbondale.
